en: Arjuna said: Out of kindness to me you spoke the highest secret teaching about the Self. Through your words my confusion is gone.

first: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया ।
en: Lotus-eyed one, I have heard from you in detail how beings arise and pass away, and also about your undying greatness.
Supreme Lord, it is just as you have described yourself. Still, highest Person, I wish to see your divine form.

first: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो ।
en: Lord, if you think I am able to see it, then, master of yoga, show me your undying Self.

first: पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।
en: Krishna said: See, Partha, my forms by the hundreds and thousands, many kinds of divine forms, of many colours and shapes.
See the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins and the Maruts. See many wonders, Bharata, that no one has seen before.
See now, Gudakesha, the whole world, moving and unmoving, gathered in one place here in my body, and whatever else you wish to see.

first: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा ।
en: But you cannot see me with these eyes of yours. I give you divine sight. See my power as Lord.
Sanjaya said: O King, having said this, Hari, the great master of yoga, showed Partha his supreme divine form.
It had many mouths and eyes, many wonderful sights, many divine ornaments and many divine weapons held up.
He wore divine garlands and clothes and was anointed with divine scents. He was a God full of every wonder, endless, with faces on every side.
If the light of a thousand suns were to rise in the sky all at once, it might be like the light of that great Being.
There, in the body of the God of gods, the son of Pandu then saw the whole universe in one place, with all its many divisions.
Then Dhananjaya, filled with wonder, his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the God and spoke with joined palms.
Arjuna said: God, in your body I see all the gods and the many kinds of beings, Brahma the Lord seated on the lotus, all the sages and the divine serpents.
I see you everywhere, endless in form, with many arms, bellies, mouths and eyes. Lord of the universe, whose form is the universe, I see no end, no middle and no beginning of you.
I see you with crown, mace and discus, a mass of light shining on every side, hard to look at, blazing like fire and sun, beyond all measure.
You are the undying, the highest to be known; you are the final resting place of this universe. You never change, you guard the eternal law, and I see you as the ancient Person.
I see you without beginning, middle or end, of endless strength, with countless arms, the moon and sun as your eyes, your mouth a blazing fire, heating this whole universe with your light.
The space between heaven and earth and all the directions are filled by you alone. Great One, seeing this wonderful and fearsome form of yours, the three worlds tremble.
These crowds of gods are entering into you; some, afraid, praise you with joined palms. Crowds of great sages and perfected ones cry 'May all be well!' and praise you with many hymns.
The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, the Ashvins, the Maruts, the ancestors, and crowds of Gandharvas, Yakshas, demons and perfected ones all gaze at you in amazement.
Mighty-armed one, seeing your huge form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs and feet, many bellies and many terrible teeth, the worlds tremble, and so do I.
Seeing you touching the sky, blazing in many colours, with mouths wide open and huge burning eyes, my heart shakes. Vishnu, I find no courage and no peace.
Seeing your mouths with terrible teeth, like the fire at the end of time, I lose my sense of direction and find no comfort. Be kind, Lord of gods, home of the world.
All these sons of Dhritarashtra, with crowds of kings, and Bhishma, Drona and Karna, together with the chief warriors on our side too,
are rushing into your dreadful mouths with their terrible teeth. Some are seen caught between your teeth, their heads crushed to powder.
As the many currents of rivers rush toward the ocean, so these heroes of the human world enter your blazing mouths.
As moths rush at great speed into a blazing fire to die, so these people rush at great speed into your mouths to their destruction.
Swallowing all the worlds on every side with your flaming mouths, you lick your lips. Your fierce rays fill the whole universe with light and scorch it, Vishnu.
Tell me who you are, in this fierce form. I bow to you, best of gods; be kind. I wish to know you, the first one, for I do not understand what you are doing.
Krishna said: I am Time, grown mighty, the destroyer of worlds, now at work to wipe out these people. Even without you, none of the warriors standing in the opposing armies will live.
So stand up and win glory. Defeat your enemies and enjoy a rich kingdom. I have already killed them; be only the instrument, Savyasachi.

first: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च
en: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and the other brave warriors are already killed by me. Kill them; do not be troubled. Fight, and you will defeat your rivals in battle.
Sanjaya said: Hearing these words of Keshava, the crowned Arjuna, trembling, with joined palms, bowed and spoke again to Krishna in a choked voice, deeply afraid.
Arjuna said: It is right, Hrishikesha, that the world rejoices and delights in praising you. The demons flee in fear in every direction, and all the crowds of perfected ones bow to you.

And why should they not bow to you, Great One, who are greater even than Brahma, the first creator? Endless One, Lord of gods, home of the world, you are the undying, what is and what is not, and what is beyond both.
You are the first God, the ancient Person, the final resting place of this universe. You are the knower and what is to be known, the highest home. Endless One, the universe is filled by you.
You are Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati and the great-grandfather of all. I bow to you a thousand times, and again and again I bow to you.
I bow to you in front and behind; I bow to you on every side, you who are all. Your strength is endless and your power has no measure. You fill everything, so you are everything.
Thinking of you as a friend, I spoke rashly, calling 'O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend', not knowing your greatness, out of carelessness or out of affection.
And if in jest I showed you disrespect while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, Achyuta, I ask you, the boundless one, to forgive me.

You are the father of this world of moving and unmoving things, the one it worships, the greatest teacher. No one is equal to you in the three worlds; how could anyone be greater, you of matchless power?
So I bow down, lay my body before you, and ask your grace, Lord worthy of praise. As a father with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved, please bear with me, God.
I am thrilled to have seen what was never seen before, yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me that other form of yours, God. Be kind, Lord of gods, home of the world.
I wish to see you as before, with crown, mace and discus in hand. Thousand-armed one, whose body is the universe, take again that four-armed form.
Krishna said: Arjuna, pleased with you, I have shown you through my own power this highest form, made of light, universal, endless and first, which no one but you has seen before.
Not by the Vedas, sacrifices or study, not by gifts, rituals or hard austerities can I be seen in this form in the human world by anyone but you, hero of the Kurus.

first: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो
en: Do not be afraid or confused at seeing this terrible form of mine. Free from fear and glad at heart, look once more at my familiar form.
Sanjaya said: Having spoken this way to Arjuna, Vasudeva showed his own form again. Taking once more his gentle shape, the Great One comforted the frightened Arjuna.

first: दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन ।
en: Arjuna said: Janardana, seeing this gentle human form of yours, I am calm again and have returned to my normal self.
Krishna said: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see. Even the gods always long to see it.

first: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया ।
en: Not by the Vedas, not by austerity, not by gifts and not by sacrifice can I be seen as you have seen me.
But by devotion to me alone, Arjuna, I can be known in this way, seen as I truly am, and entered into, Parantapa.
Whoever works for me, holds me as the highest, is devoted to me, free from attachment and without hatred toward any being, comes to me, son of Pandu.
